test_title: PYST 8: SSC CPO - English Comprehension (Held On 12 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question: Choose the correct direct sentence of the following sentence. He said that the committee had decided to postpone the event.

options.text: He said, "The committee has decided to postpone the event."
He said, "The committee had decided to postpone the event."
He said, "The event was postponed by the committee."
He said, "The committee would postpone the event."

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ 
• **Given Sentence Analysis:** The sentence is in indirect speech and uses the past perfect tense to describe a decision made by the committee. 
• **Conversion to Direct Speech:** 
• The reporting verb "said" is retained as it is. 
• The tense of the reported speech ('had decided') reverts to the present perfect ('has decided') in direct speech. 
• The quotation marks are added to enclose the direct speech. 
• The pronouns and word order remain the same as the given sentence is already in the correct format for conversion. 
• **Correct Format:** 
• Direct speech begins with a capital letter and ends with appropriate punctuation. 
• Quotation marks are used to enclose the spoken words. Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**. **Correct Sentence:** *He said, "The committee has decided to postpone the event."* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 
• **Option 2:** "The committee had decided to postpone the event." 
• Incorrect tense: In standard Indirect to Direct conversion, the past perfect tense typically reverts to the present perfect tense rather than remaining unchanged. 
• **Option 3:** "The event was postponed by the committee." 
• Incorrect structure: The sentence changes from active to passive voice, altering the meaning. 
• **Option 4:** "The committee would postpone the event." 
• Incorrect tense: "would postpone" indicates a future possibility, which does not align with the past perfect tense of the original sentence. </ul
